reasoning: A hybrid strategy combines autonomous reasoning to identify obvious shared features across misclassified instances with external XAI tools to quantify feature importance and detect spurious correlations. This ensures both pattern recognition and statistical validation of feature relevance, especially for features that may appear common but are not semantically meaningful. Given the high number of misclassifications and shared attributes, using both reasoning and tool-based attribution enhances detection accuracy.

autonomous_tasks.query: Identify which columns are present in all three misclassified instances (13590, 2021, 31974) and assess their semantic relevance to income prediction.
autonomous_tasks.expected_output: A list of shared feature names across all instances that are not semantically related to income class (e.g., education-num=9, marital-status=Married-civ-spouse, relationship=Husband)

autonomous_tasks.query: Evaluate whether the shared features like 'marital-status=Married-civ-spouse' or 'relationship=Husband' might act as spurious correlations by being strongly present in misclassified instances with the same predicted class (<=50K) despite no direct link to income.
autonomous_tasks.expected_output: Insight into whether shared features introduce false signal due to bias or data leakage.

tool_selection.reasoning: SHAP provides robust, model-agnostic feature importance scores across instances, allowing us to identify which features drive predictions with high attribution in the misclassified cases. LIME and Integrated Gradients offer local interpretability to verify spurious influence. Sensitivity analysis helps isolate how changes in shared features affect predictions, confirming whether they are driving misclassification despite lack of semantic relevance. Together, these tools validate and cross-check the autonomous findings, ensuring a comprehensive detection of shared spurious features.
